message.content: The last common ancestor of the clade that includes the families **Felidae** (lions) and **Equidae** (zebras), which is the ancestor of the clade that includes the orders **Carnivora** and **Perissodactyla**, lived roughly 70 million years ago.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor of lion and zebra. We need to answer. This is a biology question. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga). Both are mammals, specifically within the order Carnivora for lion and order Perissodactyla for zebra. Actually zebra is an equid, order Perissodactyla. Lion is a felid, order Carnivora. So their common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Or maybe more specific: the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria group? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of the superorder Laurasiatheria. Within Laurasiatheria, the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla would be the ancestor of the clade that includes the orders that diverged into the two groups. But we can say the last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the families Felidae and Equidae. That might be the ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That ancestor would have lived around 70 million years ago. So the answer: the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the ancestor of the Laurasiatheria. Alternatively, we could mention the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. So the answer: the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That ancestor lived about 70 million years ago.
